title: Taken by one of the big four: Snakebite at Maharashtra tribal school
author: Vinaya Deshpande Pandit
content_html:
Eight-year-old Anu Koreti’s eyes twinkled as she raved about the performances put together to celebrate World Tribal Day on August 9. She clapped to the dance performances and later raved to her older brother about how much she had enjoyed them. That was the last conversation she had before going to bed at a tribal residential school in Dhanora, Gadchiroli district, in Maharashtra. The programme honoured tribal culture, and gave a call for tribal empowerment.

For Anu and her two older siblings studying here, their only hope for a better future away from poverty was this tribal residential school. For them, and for the two generations of Gonds, a Scheduled Tribe, who studied in the private, aided primary and secondary Ashram School in Japtalai in Dhanora, empowerment meant a window to education.

title: Retrofitting Tamil Nadu to strike at drug menace
author: S. Vijay Kumar
content_html:
The Tamil Nadu Police have launched a multi-pronged strategy to eradicate substance abuse in the State. The launch of a new force, Anti Narcotics Task Force (ANTF), does not seem to be just another initiative in rhetoric but a concerted effort to end the prevalence of drugs, especially ganja, by taking on drug syndicates, smugglers, and others involved in the high-stakes illegal business.

Three months after the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) assumed power, it has taken the first big step towards fulfilling Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay’s election promise that he would end the drug culture in the State.

Since May 10 this year, 5,082 drug-related cases have been registered in the State and 7,214 suspects have been arrested on the charges of trafficking, possession, and distribution of drugs. More than 7,000 kg of ganja, 112 kg of other drugs, and 3.4 lakh tablets (prescribed drugs obtained without authorisation) were seized.

The special force has been formed in the wake of reports of youth, including college students, getting addicted to ganja and drugs such as methamphetamine or meth, a highly addictive synthetic stimulant, freely available in rave parties. The link between crime and drug addiction is also proven. It is in this context that the government constituted the ANTF, involving multiple stakeholders and law-enforcement agencies.

Though attempts were made in the past to dismantle inter-State drug syndicates and neutralise their supply chain and manpower, the unlawful activity continued to thrive with the suspects adopting newer means of transport and distribution. Even as the State police managed to curtail ganja cultivation in the tri-junction forest area of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, the flow of the drug continues from Andhra Pradesh and Odisha.

After intensive search operations on train and road routes along inter-State borders, smugglers have stopped moving ganja in large quantities. Now, they engage small-time peddlers to smuggle less than 4 kg to 5 kg per consignment, mostly by train.

Flowing from neighbouring States

While the Narcotics Intelligence Bureau-Criminal Investigation Department (NIB-CID) and the local police have been working in coordination with Central agencies, such as the Narcotics Control Bureau, to contain the prevalence of drugs, the efforts did not yield the desired result. The police suspect that the inflow of ganja or marijuana or cannabis continues from neighbouring States, Andhra Pradesh in particular. Besides local consumption, ganja and other synthetic drugs are smuggled to Sri Lanka with the help of illegal boat operators for further transhipment to South-East Asian countries.

The high-capacity ANTF is a dedicated force. It was born out of a major overhaul of the State’s strategy to combat drug trafficking and substance abuse aimed at achieving a ‘Drug-Free Tamil Nadu’. The new architecture, sanctioned through a Government Order issued on August 8 this year, seeks to replace the existing enforcement framework with a dedicated, technology-driven, and intelligence-led system. The initiative combines specialised policing with financial investigations, cyber-surveillance, treatment and rehabilitation of drug addicts, youth engagement, and community participation.

It seeks to significantly expand the State’s dedicated anti-narcotics field force by strengthening it with technology. As many as 65 specialised ANTF police stations have been sanctioned; they will cover 37 police districts and eight city police commissionerates. Each of these stations will have one Inspector of Police, four Sub-Inspectors, and 20 police personnel. Together, they will provide 1,625 dedicated personnel for field-level narcotics enforcement across Tamil Nadu.

Not meant for routine policing

A key feature of the new arrangement is that ANTF personnel would not be deployed for routine policing to make sure that the force remains an exclusive deployment agency tasked to maintain sustained surveillance, intelligence-gathering, and investigation of organised drug trafficking networks.

Before the creation of the dedicated ANTF, narcotics enforcement was largely handled by 15 NIB-CID units that functioned under the Enforcement Bureau-CID. While these units played an important role in preventing and detecting narcotics offences, the government realised that the relatively limited manpower and infrastructure available with the 15 NIB-CID units had made it difficult to maintain continuous State-wide surveillance and penetrate sophisticated trafficking networks.

What was needed was a sufficiently strong centralised headquarters with specialised capabilities for State-wide intelligence analysis, cyber-analytics, darknet monitoring, and financial investigation. But none of this was present; the NIB-CID largely relied on local police for intensive combing operations. Further, personnel attached to the local police stations were required to deal with law-and-order duties, regular crime investigation, and other responsibilities. This often limited the sustained attention that could be devoted to organised narcotics networks. However, the ANTF intends to overcome these hurdles and address these gaps through a centralised command structure and specialised field units.

The ANTF headquarters will be headed by an Additional Director-General of Police and an Inspector-General of Police, assisted by two Superintendents of Police (SP-I for Operations and SP-II for Intelligence and Administration). The headquarters will have 10 specialised wings to integrate intelligence, investigation, technology, operations, legal support, and administration.

Among the key components is a dedicated cyber lab equipped to undertake digital forensics, mobile-data extraction, darknet monitoring, open-source intelligence, and cryptocurrency and blockchain analysis.

A centralised crime records bureau will profile drug offenders, track repeat offenders, map trafficking routes, and identify drug hotspots. A special operations and investigation unit will focus on high-value cases, synthetic drug laboratories, international connections, and complex darknet distribution networks. Field intelligence units will collect information on cultivation sources, inter-State transit corridors, and maritime and coastal smuggling routes.

Legal team to help in searches

The ANTF will also have a dedicated legal unit to provide guidance on search and seizure procedures, investigation, filing of chargesheets, and trial proceedings. A 24x7 control room and helpline will provide real-time operational coordination. The police have solicited information from members of the public on drug-related offenders through the designated toll-free number 10581, while a WhatsApp chatbot facility will be available on 9498410581.

“One of the most significant changes in the State’s anti-narcotics strategy will be a greater emphasis on financial investigation. Instead of limiting enforcement to the seizure of drugs and arrest of individuals involved in street-level distribution, the ANTF will identify the financial networks supporting organised trafficking,” says Director-General of Police and Head of the Police Force Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal.

Investigators would trace illicit financial flows, identify key players and alleged kingpins, and pursue the freezing and attachment of movable and immovable properties belonging to traffickers and their accomplices under applicable legal provisions. “The objective is to weaken the financial foundations of organised drug syndicates and make trafficking increasingly difficult and unprofitable,” Dr. Aggarwal said.

Going all out: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay has taken significant steps to stamp out drugs in line with his election promise. In June, he administered a pledge against drug abuse in Chennai. | Photo Credit: B. JOTHI RAMALINGAM

Realising that policing and seizures alone cannot eliminate substance abuse, the government has roped in other departments. The Health and Family Welfare Department will establish protocols for referring first-time and small-quantity drug users for medical treatment, counselling, and rehabilitation. The government also plans to strengthen de-addiction centres, relapse tracking, case-management systems, and drug-testing facilities at district hospitals. Periodic district-level surveys have been envisaged to assess drug-use patterns and demographics for more effective healthcare interventions.

The School Education and Higher Education Departments will integrate awareness of substance abuse into educational programmes and strengthen Anti-Drug Clubs and Student Police Cadets on school and college campuses. Student volunteers from the NSS and the NCC would be mobilised as ‘Anti-Drug Warriors’. Sports competitions would be conducted regularly across the State to encourage young people to participate in constructive activities and discourage drug abuse.

When the Chief Minister administered a pledge against drug abuse in Chennai recently, about 2,000 students took part. More than one crore people joined the event online by logging into the Drug Free Tamil Nadu application. The government has also involved the Rural Development and Municipal Administration Departments to help create village- and ward-level anti-drug committees to strengthen community vigilance. Local bodies that have achieved ‘Drug-Free Village’ or ‘Drug-Free Ward’ status will receive State-level recognition and incentives.

The Information and Public Relations Department, the publicity arm of the government, will coordinate sustained public awareness campaigns, social media outreach, and community engagement programmes. The aim is not only to increase awareness of the dangers of drugs but also to encourage public reporting and reduce the stigma associated with seeking treatment.

The new framework also provides for a structured system of monitoring and accountability. At the district level, weekly reviews would be chaired by the Collector, along with the District Superintendent of Police or the City Police Commissioner and the local body administrative heads. At the State level, fortnightly reviews would be chaired by the ADGP (ANTF) to assess field operations and tactical progress.

Apex review every month

An apex review will be held every month under the chairmanship of the Chief Secretary. It will focus on coordination among departments, implementation of policy measures, and the overall impact of the anti-narcotics programme. The Chief Minister will be apprised of the outcome of filed operations, seizures, and overall progress and impact of the ANTF on a fortnightly basis, according to police sources.

The government expects the ANTF to mark a shift from conventional drug seizures towards dismantling entire trafficking networks. By combining dedicated manpower with cyber-capabilities, intelligence-gathering, financial investigation, and inter-departmental action, Tamil Nadu aims to tackle both the supply of narcotics and the demand for drugs.

The broader objective is to neutralise organised trafficking networks, protect children and young people, improve access to treatment and rehabilitation, and strengthen community participation in preventing substance abuse — ultimately paving the way for a safer and healthier ‘Drug-Free Tamil Nadu’.

title: U.P. CM Yogi Adityanath announces new ‘Youth Policy’ on Independence Day
author: Mayank Kumar
content_html:
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday (August 15, 2026) announced a new ‘Youth Policy’ for the youth of Uttar Pradesh and described youth power as the State’s greatest strength.

At the state-level Independence Day celebration organised at Vidhan Bhavan, Mr. Adityanath said, “Today, I am extremely pleased to announce that through the ‘Youth Policy’, we will succeed in further strengthening the skill, innovation and employment of the youth of the state through an integrated approach. The government’s resolve is to put skill, innovation and employment in the hands of every youth. The resolve to make proper use of the capabilities and potential of the youth will be given further momentum.”

The upcoming policy is likely to focus on skill development, employment generation, Artificial Intelligence (AI) and entrepreneurship, under a dedicated mechanism.

Mr. Adityanath described youth power as Uttar Pradesh’s greatest strength, adding, “the state’s youth are talented, hard-working and full of the determination to achieve something for the country and society. The strength of Uttar Pradesh lies in the talent of its youth. The government has taken strict action against the cheating mafia and recruitment mafia, and the state’s demographic dividend is being transformed into a ‘development engine’.” 

The CM further highlighted the improvement in law and order in U.P., under the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) rule. “With this historic improvement in law and order, Uttar Pradesh has now transformed from Upadrav Pradesh (State of Unrest) to Utsav Pradesh (State of Celebrations). Uttar Pradesh, once counted among the BIMARU states, is today playing the role of the ‘growth engine’ of the country’s economy. By ending policy paralysis, the state has been established as a ‘dream destination’ for investment,” he said. 

The Chief Minister added, “Today, our sisters and daughters can go to the market at any time, go alone for their studies, return home from work and fulfil their dreams. Over the past 9 years, along with ensuring due respect for women’s power, they have also been given freedom from insecurity.”

Mr. Adityanath further said, “We are building an Uttar Pradesh where there is heritage as well as the technology of the future. Where the pride of culture and the pace of modernity will move together, the roots of tradition will remain strong, and the wings of development will be seen touching the sky.”

title: Teenager electrocuted while fixing Tricolour at Madhya Pradesh school
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
A 17-year-old boy was electrocuted on Friday (August 14, 2026) while he was fixing the National Flag for the Independence Day celebrations at a private school in Madhya Pradesh.

According to the police, the incident took place on Friday afternoon (August 14, 2026) at Little Star Public School in Datia town. The student, Raj Kushwaha, was called by school officials after school hours and sent to the rooftop to install the National Flag on a pole for the Independence Day celebrations.

Datia Superintendent of Police Mayur Khandelwal told The Hindu that an FIR has been registered against the school officials under relevant provisions, including Section 105 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).

Mr. Khandelwal said that the boy suffered burns after coming into contact with an 11 KV power line passing over the school roof. He died on the spot.

“We have initiated a probe into the matter and are questioning people at the school,” he said.

Family members of Mr. Kushwaha staged a demonstration, alleging that the school management failed to inform them of the incident immediately. The protest caused a traffic jam on NH-44. Cabinet Minister Narayan Singh Kushwaha, whose convoy was caught in the jam, spoke to the victim’s family and assured them of police action.

In another incident, two school students died on Saturday (August 15, 2026) in Rewa district after drowning in a water-filled pit next to a government school ground while returning from an Independence Day programme.

title: Don’t make statements that BJP can exploit, Akhilesh Yadav tells Samajwadi Party leaders
author: The Hindu Bureau
content_html:
The Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav cautioned party leaders on Saturday (August 15, 2026) against making statements that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) could exploit.

“No statement should be made that the BJP can exploit. We will print a pamphlet for every leader.., instructing them to speak only from this material. Don’t speak otherwise,” cautioned Mr. Yadav, addressing an Independence Day event at the state party headquarters.

Mr. Yadav was reacting to the SP leader Shivpal Singh Yadav's statement that Azam Khan would be the State’s Home Minister when their party comes to power. This led to Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath questioning the statement and alleging that the SP want to trigger riots again in U.P.

Mr. Adityanath, without naming Shivpal Singh Yadav or Azam Khan, said, “The Samajwadi Party is standing behind a person who built a university (Jauhar University at Rampur) after an individual (Mohammad Ali Jauhar) responsible for India’s Partition and who opposed the country’s Independence. They are saying that if their party comes to power, they will make him the Home Minister.” The U.P. CM added, “Just look at their thinking. This means they want to trigger riots again.”

Shivpal Singh Yadav made the statement after visiting Mr. Khan in jail.

Mr. Adityanath, without naming Shivpal Singh Yadav or Azam Khan, said, “The Samajwadi Party is standing behind a person who built a university (Jauhar University at Rampur) after an individual (Mohammad Ali Jauhar) responsible for India’s Partition and who opposed the country’s Independence. They are saying that if their party comes to power, they will make him the Home Minister.” The U.P. CM added, “Just look at their thinking. This means they want to trigger riots again.”
Shivpal Singh Yadav made the statement after visiting Mr. Khan in jail.

title: With slogans and tears, Ujjain schoolgirls protest plan to shift government schools far away
author: Mehul Malpani
content_html:
Hundreds of school girls in Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain have come out in protest against plans to merge and shift various government schools in which they study to Daudkhedi, a location about six-10 kilometres from their respective schools, and out of the city limits. 

On Friday (August 14, 2026), more than 300 girls of an all-girls school from the Sarafa area of Ujjain, accompanied by parents and activists, staged a demonstration at the Collector’s office against the government’s plans, while raising concerns for their safety and commute, as several students hail from nearby rural pockets. While students wearing their school uniforms staged a sit-in and raised slogans for nearly two hours, many were also seen breaking into tears and making emotional appeals to the authorities. Two girls also fainted during the protests, the protestors said. 

At least six middle and secondary schools from areas including Sarafa, Mahakal Maidan, Maharajwada, and Jaisinghpura are likely to be impacted under the State government’s ongoing measures to merge smaller schools into larger schools, such as the Sandipani schools, earlier known as the flagship CM Rise schools. 

Activists involved with the protests claim the six schools are proposed to be merged with the Sandipani Vidyalaya, built in Daudkhedi, and that the move is likely to impact more than 2,500 students. 

The students also appeared to be taking inspiration from the Gen Z protests that stormed the national capital of New Delhi in July, and ended with the resignation of the then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Shikha (name changed to protect identity), a student, said that many girls already travel about 8-10 km and that their parents were concerned about travelling further away now. 

“The way Gen Z protested in Delhi and the government had to bend before them, we will also carry out a movement here and will give up food and water if it comes to that. We just want education, which is our right. They started the scheme ‘Beti Bachao Beti Padhao’, but how will the daughter go so far when her parents are labourers?” Ms. Shikha said.

She also alleged that they had written to the Collector requesting him to meet the students but “only lower-level officials were coming”.

Nutan (name changed to protect identity), another student, spoke of distances and safety issues. “We don’t want to go to Daudkhedi. Our current school is on the main road and many of us come from very far-away villages. If we go there (Daudkhedi), which is very far, who will take responsibility for our safety? Two girls fainted here because we have not eaten anything since morning,” Ms. Nutan said.

“Some of us are not well. We have not eaten anything since morning but nobody is listening to us here. Have some shame,” a girl who broke down in tears during the protests said. A teacher also appeared emotional while trying to console the girl.

Following a meeting with parents and activists, Ujjain District Education Officer Mahendra Khatri said that the decision to shift the schools has not yet been taken, and that the final decision would be taken by the district-level monitoring committee, which is expected to meet next week. 

“We have forwarded the note sheet from our side. The meeting should take place by Wednesday (August 19, 2026). During the meeting, the representatives of the students will be informed [about the proposal] and they can put forth their views,” Mr. Khatri said, adding that the Sarafa school would continue to function from its current location till a decision is taken. 

Jitendra Sengar, an activist with the School Bachao Sangharsh Samiti that is backing the student protests, said students from various schools facing the impact have staged demonstrations against the move in July, and written applications had been given to authorities four times. 

“We have no problem with new Sandipani schools. But if you shut down all schools within a 15-km radius, and only run one, it is a violation of the Right to Education Act. While the children of the rich, politicians, and senior officials will study in the city, it is the students from poor backgrounds who will be impacted by this move,” Mr. Sengar said. 

“Parents of many of these students are labourers and the increased distance will hamper their earnings too, as several parents will have to drop their kids to school,” he said, claiming that all six schools were established before 1960. 

As per a recent government order, 11 schools of the district, of which six are in urban areas, are proposed to be merged and shifted to Daudkhedi, Mr. Sengar said. 

Mr. Khatri denied that the students had already submitted their written protest at least four times in the recent past. “The matter has come to my attention for the first time,” he said.
